    A line in a critical quotient #

    Let D be a directed algebra whose arrows join points with no third point between them, with one-dimensional corners. Let Λ = D / ⟨e_v : v ∉ T'⟩ have a critical Euler form in at least ten variables, rigid modules off each point and a sincere directing module. The Euler form has an induced path through all points of T' but two (UnitForm.Critical.longPath). Along it:

    • consecutive points are joined by an arrow of D: a brick of dimension vector e_a + e_b exists (exists_brick_off), and without an arrow its support would split (not_isIndecMod_of_split);
    • other points are not joined by an arrow: an arrow is a full edge (eulerForm_c_quot_interval);
    • the brick with dimension vector the indicator of the path, restricted to D, is an indecomposable D-module with one-dimensional spaces on the path, zero elsewhere, and every arrow of the path acts on it (again by not_isIndecMod_of_split).

    This is exists_critical_line.
